questiontext.text:
Goal

Write two functions, one that prints numbers from range and one that prints the names in a list.

How this works in Python

Java gives you two ways to walk a sequence. One counts with an index. The other takes each element in turn.

for (int i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
    System.out.println(i);
}
for (String site : sites) {
    System.out.println(site);
}

Python keeps only the second shape. The counted form for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) is not part of the language, and no amount of searching will turn it up.

for site in sites:
    print(site)

Read that as "for each site in sites". The loop variable needs no declaration and no type, and Python binds it again on every pass. You are handed the value, never the position.

When you want numbers, ask range for them.

  • range(3) hands you 0, 1 and 2. The stop value is never included.
  • range(n) therefore runs the body n times, and range(0) runs it not at all.

A list is Python's growable sequence, written with square brackets, as in ["north", "east"]. It is the closest thing to an ArrayList. A for loop walks a list directly, with no index and no call to fetch an element.

In Python def starts a function, so def channel_ids(n): declares a function called channel_ids that takes one argument named n.

The Java habit to break here is reaching for the index. If your first instinct was range(len(sites)), that instinct is the whole reason this question exists.

Your task
  • Replace each comment in the answer box with a body, indented four spaces under its header.
  • channel_ids(n) prints every number from 0 up to but not including n, one per line.
  • list_sites(sites) prints every name in the list sites, one per line, in order.

Each body is one loop and one print. You pass when each function prints those lines and nothing else.

Rules
  • Do not write range(len(...)). Walk the list itself.
  • Do not index the list. sites[0] is banned.
  • Do not create a counter of your own. No i = i + 1 and no +=. The loop supplies the values.
  • Write for in both bodies. while is off limits here.
Before you click Check

Write down what you expect each test to print. Then run it. A surprise means your model of Python is wrong, and that is the part worth learning.

AI protocol

No AI. Type every character yourself. This tier builds the muscle, and a tool that types it for you skips the exercise.

testcode.text: channel_ids(1) list_sites([]) list_sites(["solo"]) print("edge cases done")

import inspect counted = inspect.getsource(channel_ids) walked = inspect.getsource(list_sites) whole = counted + walked assert "range(len" not in whole, "rule broken: no range(len(...))" assert "while" not in whole, "rule broken: both loops must be a for" assert "+=" not in whole, "rule broken: the loop supplies the values" assert "= i + 1" not in whole, "rule broken: no counter of your own" assert "range(" in counted, "rule broken: count with range" assert "[" not in walked, "rule broken: never index the list" channel_ids(2) list_sites(["alpha"])

questiontext.text:
Goal

Write four functions that print squares, a countdown, a labelled channel list, and a range object.

How this works in Python

Java gives you two loops for walking a sequence. One counts with an index. The other takes each element in turn.

for (int i = 1; i <= 5; i++) {
    System.out.println(i * i);
}
for (String name : names) {
    System.out.println("CH: " + name);
}

Python has only the second shape. The counted form for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) does not exist anywhere in the language.

for name in names:
    print("CH:", name)

Read that as "for each name in names". The loop variable needs no declaration and no type. Python binds it fresh on every pass and hands you the value, never the position.

To count, ask range for the numbers.

  • range(5) gives 0, 1, 2, 3, 4. The stop value is never included.
  • range(1, 6) gives 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. The first value is the start.
  • range(5, 0, -1) gives 5, 4, 3, 2, 1. The third value is the step, and a negative step counts down.

range is not an array. It produces each number only when the loop asks for one, so printing it shows range(0, 3) rather than the numbers. Wrap it in list(...) to pull the numbers out.

A list is Python's growable sequence, written with square brackets, as in ["north", "east"]. It is the closest thing to an ArrayList.

The first lines topic taught the colon header and the indented block. A loop body follows those same two rules.

Your task
  • Replace each comment in the answer box with a body, indented four spaces under its header. Every body is one loop or one call.
  • squares_to_five() prints the square of each number from 1 to 5, one per line. The first argument to range is the start value.
  • countdown_from(start) prints start down to 1 inclusive, one per line, using a negative step. The step is the third argument to range.
  • label_channels(names) prints CH: and then the name, once for every name in the list. Use print("CH:", name) so the space lands in the right place.
  • show_range() prints the range(3) object beside list(range(3)) with one call to print. The output is range(0, 3) [0, 1, 2].

You pass when each function prints its lines in order and adds nothing else.

Rules
  • Do not write i += 1 or i = i + 1. The loop supplies the values.
  • Do not index the list. names[0] is banned and so is range(len(names)).
  • Write for in all three loops. while is off limits in this one.
  • Do not create a counter variable of your own.
Before you click Check

Write down what you expect each test to print. Then run it. A surprise means your model of Python is wrong, and that is the part worth learning.

AI protocol

AI for explanation only. Ask it what an error means or why one form is more idiomatic. Do not let it write your answer.

expected.text: CH: north CH: east CH: vertical range(0, 3) [0, 1, 2]

testcode.text: countdown_from(1) label_channels([]) label_channels(["solo"]) print("edge cases done")

import inspect whole = inspect.getsource(squares_to_five) + inspect.getsource(countdown_from) + inspect.getsource(label_channels) assert "while" not in whole, "rule broken: every loop here must be a for" assert "+=" not in whole, "rule broken: the loop supplies the values" assert "= n + 1" not in whole and "= i + 1" not in whole, "rule broken: the loop supplies the values" assert "range(len" not in whole, "rule broken: no range(len(...))" assert "[" not in inspect.getsource(label_channels), "rule broken: never index the list" assert "for " in inspect.getsource(countdown_from), "rule broken: use a for loop" countdown_from(2) show_range()

name.text: WAT 02.3: The Loop Grew an Else!

questiontext.text:
Goal

Write three loop functions, one that stops on a sentinel, one that uses break and continue, and one that uses a for ... else clause.

How this works in Python

So far the loop has handed you every value and asked nothing else of you. Some loops cannot work that way, because they do not know in advance how many passes they need.

Java's while repeats for as long as a condition holds. Python's does the same, without the parentheses and with a colon on the end.

int index = 0;
while (readings[index] != -1) {
    System.out.println("reading " + readings[index]);
    index++;
}
index = 0
while readings[index] != -1:
    print("reading", readings[index])
    index = index + 1

Two things carry over from that pair. Python has no ++ and no --, so you write index = index + 1 in full. And readings[index] reads one element by position, counting from 0, the same way a Java array does.

A value that means "stop here" is a sentinel. The loop above stops when it reads -1, not when it runs out of elements. A sentinel loop is the one place an index of your own belongs. Every other loop in this topic shows why for is the default.

break leaves the loop at once. continue abandons the current pass and starts the next one. Both behave as they do in Java.

Then the surprise. A Python loop can carry an else clause, and Java has nothing that matches it.

for code in codes:
    if code > 100:
        print("fault", code)
        break
else:
    print("all clear")

The else belongs to the for, not to the if. Read the indentation, because else sits at the same depth as for. It runs when the loop reaches the end of the sequence without meeting a break, and it is skipped when a break fires. An empty list runs it too, because a loop over nothing reaches the end without breaking.

The keyword is misleading and almost everyone reads it wrong the first time. Read it as "no break" rather than "else". It exists to retire the search flag, the boolean found = false that Java makes you declare, set inside the loop and test underneath it. A while loop takes the same clause on the same terms.

Your task
  • drain(readings) walks a list of ints with a while loop and an index of its own. For each reading before the sentinel it prints reading and then the value. When it meets the sentinel -1 it stops the loop and prints sentinel reached. Every list handed to it holds a -1 somewhere, so the loop always has a way out. Anything sitting after the sentinel is left unread.
  • scan(codes) walks a list of ints with a for loop. It skips a 0 with continue and prints nothing for it. It prints abort and leaves with break on the first negative value. Any other value it prints as code and then the value.
  • find_fault(codes) walks a list of ints with a for loop. On the first value above 100 it prints fault and then the value, then breaks. When no value is above 100 it prints all clear once, from the loop's own else clause. That else sits at the same indentation as the for.

Write print("reading", value), print("code", value) and print("fault", value) so the space lands in the right place. You pass when each function prints its lines in order and adds nothing else.

Rules
  • Write while in drain, with an index of your own. A for loop there fails the checker.
  • Stop drain on the sentinel. Do not call len.
  • Use both continue and break in scan.
  • Write the for ... else clause in find_fault and carry no found flag. The words True and False are banned inside that function.
Before you click Check

Write down what you expect each test to print. Then run it. A surprise means your model of Python is wrong, and that is the part worth learning.

AI protocol

AI allowed, on three conditions. Write your plan before you open it. Read every suggestion and reject the ones you did not plan. Type accepted code out yourself rather than pressing Tab.

expected.text: reading 12 reading 7 sentinel reached sentinel reached
code 3 code 5 abort fault 120 all clear

testcode.text: drain([5, -1, 99]) scan([0, 0]) scan([-1, 4]) find_fault([]) find_fault([101]) print("edge cases done")

expected.text: reading 5 sentinel reached abort all clear fault 101 edge cases done

testcode.text: import inspect sentinel = inspect.getsource(drain) filtered = inspect.getsource(scan) searched = inspect.getsource(find_fault) assert "while" in sentinel, "rule broken: drain must use a while loop" assert "for " not in sentinel, "rule broken: drain must use a while loop" assert "len(" not in sentinel, "rule broken: stop on the sentinel, not on a length" assert "continue" in filtered, "rule broken: skip the zero with continue" assert "break" in filtered, "rule broken: stop on the negative with break" assert "for " in searched, "rule broken: find_fault must use a for loop" assert "else" in searched, "rule broken: use the for ... else clause" assert "True" not in searched and "False" not in searched, "rule broken: no found flag, the else clause replaces it" drain([8, -1]) scan([2, 0, -5, 3]) find_fault([200])

expected.text: reading 8 sentinel reached code 2 abort fault 200
